element: Profession families (F1-F15) as the unit of mobility analysis
v1_location: Dimension Tags F1-F15; Profession Family View; profession_family_definitions.md
rationale: Families are disciplinary identities, not jobs or sector-actor contexts, so family similarity cannot answer the charter's question (movement between federal, state, local, Tribal, NGO, private and academic). The CM computation finds a two-island structure: a biophysical/field-science cluster (F1-F7, F10, F12) and a statecraft/human-systems cluster (F8, F9, F11, F13-F15) with ZERO pairs above chance between them (33 above-chance pairs, all within clusters; partition identical in 150/150 Louvain runs). Keep families as navigation groupings of role profiles (agrees with CA); compute mobility on role profiles with sector-actor variants

element: Core tag definition ('a meaningful gap'; boundary tests for distinctiveness)
rationale: For mobility use, Core encodes what is DISTINCTIVE to a professional identity, so Core-only similarity systematically understates transferability by design. Core-only rankings correlate only 0.51 (Spearman) with Core+Supporting rankings. v2 role profiles need importance and level per task, not distinctiveness, so overlap measures reflect what the job actually requires

Supporting tags carry most of the transferability signal (structure is stable at Supporting weight 0.25-0.75, Spearman >=0.99) but were assigned by one analyst with an LLM and no reliability check. Do not migrate as role requirements; use only as a prior to be re-elicited with importance ratings

v1_location: Dimension Tags Zero Core; Foundational Professional Prep
rationale: The idea is right and matters for mobility: 3.1.1-3.1.3 (project planning, budget, risk) are Core in no family yet Supporting in 10, the broadest portable foundation in v1. Re-express as a computed breadth/portability score on role profiles (agrees with CA's 'compute, don't store'). Note that 2 of the 3 carry CLD flags

The seven D7 competencies are the top 7 bridges (54% of 'cross-community core bridges'). Carry them into the transversal layer, but do not cite their bridging as evidence of portability: they were tagged across many families by design (Feb 2026), so the bridging is partly constructed

v1_location: Competencies: Public Agencies | Private Sector | NGOs | Consulting | Academia
rationale: Agrees with CA (retire structure, keep as seed text). Mobility-specific addition: all 1,110 cells are populated, so every competency claims to apply in every sector. The notes carry zero discriminating information for transferability and cannot be used to compute sector-actor similarity

element: CLD (career-ladder destruction) flag and R9 severity
v1_location: Dimension Tags T13 CLD Flag / CLD Severity; CLD Signal Register
rationale: Carry the concept and compute it per pathway (agrees with CA). Mobility linkage v1 did not draw: CLD concentrates where portability is highest. 37% of SC-primary competencies are flagged vs 20-22% FC/DC; 50% of 'broad foundation' competencies; 36% of the top-25 bridges vs 28% overall. Entry tasks that teach the most portable skills are the most compressed, so CLD is also a mobility risk indicator

Needed for entry and progression links on role profiles and for pathway-level CLD (metric M-19). Extend it with sector-actor variants, because entry ladders differ by actor (federal seasonal; corps; consulting junior; state trainee)

element: Craft primary/secondary as the representation of 'blends'
v1_location: Dimension Tags Craft Primary / Craft Secondary
rationale: Agrees with CA (blend profile, not classification). Computation shows blends are asymmetric. Field-management families (F1-F4, F10, F12) have even blends (evenness 0.91-0.99; e.g. Forestry FC 38/DC 38/SC 24) while statecraft-cluster families hold almost no field craft (FC 0.7-7%). The charter's 'blend of three crafts' describes field professionals, not policy, ESG, finance or education professionals in v1's tags

Agrees with CA. Mobility-specific point: validating family similarity against observed occupational flows (CPS, LEHD) needs correct SOC targets; with 7 of 15 mappings rated Low by v1 itself, flow-based validation is infeasible for half the families until role-level SOC/OPM-series/state-class crosswalks exist

element: Five Functional Positions framework (bridging competencies between information-flow positions)
rationale: A useful within-organisation mobility lens (Sensing <-> Structuring <-> Analyzing <-> Integrating <-> Deciding) that v1 never connected to its tags. Carry as a candidate work-function facet for role profiles (CA's L0) and test whether position adjacency predicts internal moves

It counts taxonomy outputs (craft distribution, Core counts, reform flags), not workforce outcomes. Replace with outcome and leading-indicator metrics (metrics_framework.csv) so the tool is held to outcomes, not deliverables

element: Fire Management <-> Land Use Planning tags
v1_location: Dimension Tags F9/F12; profession_family_definitions.md overlap notes
rationale: The family definitions name Fire <-> Planning overlap (community wildfire protection planning), yet Fire holds 0 of Land Use Planning's 13 Core competencies and similarity is below chance (z = -1.65). Either the tags omit real overlap or the overlap is in tasks v1 never wrote. Re-check in L2 with fire and planning SMEs; this is a high-demand pathway for displaced fire staff
Agrees with CA (redesign under IO). Add reserved Workforce Voice seats with ratings reported by stratum, and a usefulness veto at G1 (practitioner_panel_design.md)

element: Absence of any observed career-path data
rationale: v1 never tested a transferability claim against an observed move. Add consented career histories (panel), state HR prior-employment fields, OPM Federal Workforce Data and licensed career-history data as the validation layer for pathway claims (metric M-03)
